D2_processevent_ownership.code: for (FProperty* P = Function->DestructorLink; P; P = P->DestructorLinkNext) { if (!P->IsInContainer(Function->ParmsSize)) { P->DestroyValue_InContainer(NewStack.Locals); } else { FMemory::Memcpy(P->ContainerPtrToValuePtr<uint8>(Parms), P->ContainerPtrToValuePtr<uint8>(NewStack.Locals), ...); } }
D2_processevent_ownership.reading: The guard is `!P->IsInContainer(Function->ParmsSize)`. ONLY properties OUTSIDE the parms region (locals) are destroyed. Properties INSIDE ParmsSize -- the caller's parameters -- are memcpy'd back into the caller's buffer and are NEVER destroyed by ProcessEvent.
D2_processevent_ownership.conclusion: The caller-supplied parameter buffer, including our input FString's backing buffer, remains CALLER-OWNED. allocate -> call -> free is safe.
D2_processevent_ownership.makesoftobjectpath_retention: FSoftObjectPath(const FString& Path) { SetPath(FStringView(Path)); } (SoftObjectPath.h:51). SetPath(FWideStringView) parses the VIEW and builds FNames (interning them) plus, when present, its own SubPathString; it stores no pointer or reference into the caller's buffer. For our target there is no ':' subobject delimiter, so SubPathString stays empty. No retention.
